title: Confucius and Yan Hui's Rice
text:
Confucius and his disciples were once stranded between the states of Chen and Cai. For seven days they had no cooked food and lived on wild greens. At last his favorite disciple, Yan Hui, managed to obtain some rice and set it to cook.

As the rice was nearly done, Confucius glanced over and saw Yan Hui reach into the pot, take some of the rice with his hand and eat it. Confucius was disappointed, but he pretended not to have seen.

When the rice was ready and Yan Hui brought it to him, Confucius got up and said he had just dreamed of his late father and wanted first to offer some clean rice to the ancestors. Yan Hui answered at once that this was impossible. Some soot had fallen into the pot while it was cooking, he explained. It seemed wrong to throw away the spoiled food, so he had taken out the dirty part and eaten it himself.

Confucius sighed. "We trust our eyes, and yet our eyes are not to be trusted. We rely on our hearts, and yet our hearts are not enough. Remember this, my disciples: it is not easy to know a person."
lesson: Even what you see with your own eyes may not tell you why someone acted. Ask before you conclude, especially about people who have earned your trust.
location: Between the states of Chen and Cai (modern Henan, China)
caveat: The hardship in Chen and Cai is historical tradition, but this particular episode appears only in later texts and is likely legendary.
